answer: Only parcels entered in the waybill book travel, because the book proves which train carried which parcel and who signed for it. A ocean parcel slipped aboard without a waybill fails the book: the entry must match the train the clerk himself loaded at the cipher of the platform, and a parcel with no entry is put off at the next station. Forging a month of waybills means bribing the parcel clerk, faking three hundred entries and paying 9,700, while the saffron book in the parcel office is audited each quarter, so a parcel whose waybill was never written is returned to sender.
